why: Rule 1 clean: deg-2 junction with 2 of 2 prongs rising away - proton stops hot at 13000 (209637) and muon Bragg at 13001, prongs 136 deg apart so not the collinear trap.
Rule 1 at a deg-4 junction: seg 69032 rises monotonically to 192713 at 69039 and seg 69025 to 202125 at 69034, both away, and the 126 cm MIP track of cluster 16 ends 11 cm from it.

Only two objects in the whole event; I took the 1.5 cm blob at 206958 e/cm, five times MIP and proton-like, over the flat MIP pair. Its two ends are 1.4 cm apart and indistinguishable, so the id within the blob is a coin flip.

The 268 cm muon is flat MIP at both ends so it does not stop anywhere, yet a hot 3.8 cm stub at 174674 hangs off this end - a track that begins mid-detector next to proton-grade charge is an interaction point, and it is the most upstream candidate at z=69.8.

The 32 cm proton rises monotonically from 15000 to 220000 on the proton template and stops at 14000, so its start 14002 is the vertex; p5 confirms it, the cone opens cleanly from 1.3 cm there while the rival 14003 already has 11 cm transverse RMS in its nearest bin.

All charge lies within the last 10 cm of z; 21005 is the only junction (deg 3, one prong rising away and none rising toward it) and rule 2 puts it 8 cm upstream of the two free ends of its own cluster.

The hot charge runs continuously across 21004 - 5 cm of 125-170k on the mu side then the whole 6.7 cm p segment at 100-250k - so that is one particle stopping, split by the fitter, and the two prongs are 154 deg apart; left with 20 scattered dots I took the only proton-grade one (155431), close to a guess.
Two Bragg ends in one cluster (350000 at 15000, 150000 at 15005) and 15002 is the junction both point away from, seen as a clear V in the Z-Y projection.
Rule 1 numuCC topology: 141 cm muon with Bragg at 12000 plus an 11.6 cm proton at 150000-230000, prongs 95 deg apart and both far ends interior, so nothing entered.

Rule 1, 2 of 2 rising away: 184 cm muon and 93 cm proton (Bragg 290000 at 18008) leave it with a 46 deg opening that the principal-frame panel shows as a clean V apex, and it is the most upstream candidate at z=167.

The 32 cm prong rises monotonically from near zero to 200000 stopping at 6001 and starts at 6003, while the rival 6013 is exactly 180 deg collinear on the muon line so it is a fit kink, not a junction.

Rule 8: the largest object in the event is 3.4 cm long, there is no junction anywhere and no readable direction in any projection, so any click is as good as another - abstaining rather than inventing a reason.
A 90 cm chain of fragments runs along +z; 17002 is the deg-3 point where a 16 cm backward proton (monotone rise to 400000 at 17001) meets the forward chain, 2 of 3 prongs rising away and none toward.
Rule 8: ten faint sub-cm dots with no dQ/dx opinion, no segment longer than half a cm, and no apex or direction readable in any projection - abstaining rather than inventing a reason.
